# Typography styles (Figma)

**Canonical units: px.** Every font size in this specification is a pixel number. No value is in points (`pt`), and the validator fails on any point unit (check 6).

## Variables, Text Styles and what binds to what

| | Figma Variable | Figma Text Style |
|---|---|---|
| What it is | One named value of one type (colour, number, text, true/false), with one value per mode | A saved bundle of text properties applied to a text layer |
| Holds here | font family names, font weights, **font sizes in px** (per tier mode) | the bundle: family, weight, size, **line height %**, **letter spacing %**, case |
| Modes | Yes (font sizes have Mobile, Tablet, Desktop) | No. A style appears once; its size follows the mode when the size is bound to a variable (to verify in Figma) |
| Why not only variables | Line height and letter spacing are unitless ratios and em values on the web; Figma stores them per style as a percentage or px value, and binding a px variable to a ratio needs a per-style conversion | Why not only styles: the sizes must change by tier and stay linked to the web values |

**How they work together.** The style's family, weight and size are *bound* to variables (`font/family/*`, `font/weight/*`, `font-size/*`). Line height and letter spacing are stored in the style as percentages. Designers apply the style; the tier is chosen by setting the **Typography** mode on the frame.

## Display versus storage in Figma

- **Size** is stored and shown as px. Fluid web sizes are sampled at 360, 768 and 1280px and rounded to a whole px (deviation from the web value at those widths: at most 0.5px; between them the web size is continuous and Figma is not).
- **Weight** is stored as a number (400, 500, 600, 700) in the variable, but Figma applies a font **style name**: 400 Regular, 500 Medium, 600 SemiBold, 700 Bold. Confirm that the installed font exposes those style names (Cormorant ships static weights; DM Sans is a variable family).
- **Line height** is specified in percent (the web ratio x 100). The px equivalents below are what Figma computes (size x percent).
- **Letter spacing** is specified in percent (the web em value x 100); the px equivalent below is for the Desktop size.
- **Case**: `UPPER` is Figma's text case setting, the equivalent of `text-transform: uppercase`.
- **Font stack**: the web system lists fallback fonts; Figma has none, so the primary family only is used.

## Setting up the styles in Figma (manual; nothing here was created in Figma)
. Create the variables first (see [../../02-Design-Variables/Figma-Variables/README.md](../../02-Design-Variables/Figma-Variables/README.md)).. Create one Text Style per row, named exactly as in the table (the slash creates the folder).. In each style bind **font family**, **font weight** (or choose the matching style name) and **font size** to the named variables; type the line height and letter spacing percentages.. Set the frame's **Typography** mode to Mobile, Tablet or Desktop and check that the sizes in the preview match the table.
